scope: Independent read-only review of frozen acknowledged-seek controller fix plus manager tests. Source hashes independently verified. Standalone TypeScript fake-binding/controller tests only; no client, QQ, native compilation/execution or production edit.
result: No open P0-P2 finding in the frozen reviewed fix. This source/test result does not establish the rebuilt real-client48k/96k outcome.
baselineDiagnosis: qq-task14-paused-seek-independent-review.json preserves the older ac573ac0 diagnosis and public-vs-native-ACK evidence boundary.
specThenQualityReview: Service-mode seek now waits for actual callAsync Seek completion and a fresh callAsync GetPlaybackInfo readback before publishing a confirmed target. The direct synchronous path rejects tryNative failure instead of unconditionally publishing.

One SeekTransaction slot is bound to existing transportRevision, source, queue revision/index and native binding. New Play/Stop/queue/new Seek invalidate old ownership; crash reset clears the slot. The callbacks check ownership after waits and before publication.

Pending seeks coalesce at the controller admission boundary: an already-dispatched first request may complete, but only the latest queued intent proceeds after the predecessor completion. A rejected obsolete predecessor cannot prevent a newer explicit seek.

A dependent toggle extends only a matching transaction acceptedRevision from the previous global revision. It waits for that transaction before posting Pause. Two concurrently waiting toggles remain two toggles; newer Play/Stop/Seek cannot revive the old slot.

Pause retains its existing fast service deadline. ServiceBinding slow ownership,20-second caller deadline and separate completion grace are unchanged; there is no new utility-process scheduler or global transport queue.

Paused readback confirmation uses a single-frame bound from the actual/output/source rate. Playing confirmation allows elapsed playback and the existing buffer frame allowance. Source/queue and position finiteness are checked.

The acknowledged position is explicitly committed after the ordinary merge, with lastNativeReportedPosition set to that confirmed position. This bypasses the ordinary-tick backward suppression only for the verified transport ACK.

A failed/unconfirmed current transaction clears its presentation pending target and retains its rejected barrier. Resume fails without posting Pause until an explicit new Seek/Play/Stop changes the transport. A pending/failed same-position seek is not skipped, so retrying the actual old position can recover.

The successful resolved slot is retained as one bounded current-source record; later same-source toggles can use it. It is not an additional queue or source generation. Root/implementation descriptions should not claim successful slots are cleared immediately.

limits: The v3 trace public field called native still comes from the controller merged snapshot, not a utility-process ACK. It does not time the original48k native Seek directly.
Other unrelated synchronous slow native calls can still create service head-of-line blocking. This fix gates the owned seek prerequisite and does not introduce a general execution-start protocol.
A failed or timed-out seek intentionally keeps resume closed until explicit transport recovery; timeout is not treated as proof that child native work was canceled.

Existing renderer seek error handling and optimistic clock presentation were not changed. The main confirmed state is now honest, but real-client UI/error behavior still needs the root-owned rebuilt acceptance trace.
No real48k/96k playback, original QQ cache, packaged artifact or user-visible completion claim follows from these synthetic source gates.
